summary: Bitterroot NF lookout: a 1930 tree platform, an L-4 tower, then a 1960 R-6 cab on a concrete base; drive-up, staffed in fire season, wrapped against fires in 2013 and 2017.

events.note: First lookout: a platform in a 40-foot tree top.
Disputed: firelookout.com and Forest Lookouts date a 40-foot pole L-4 tower to 1934; the register and Idaho Fire Lookouts say 1940.
The register and Idaho Fire Lookouts date an L-4 cab on a 10-foot tower to 1940.
Earliest named staffer on Idaho Fire Lookouts' known-staff list; the list may not be complete.
Current R-6 flat-top cab on a 10-foot concrete base. A 1959 base build is also reported.
Mark and Rhett Moak staffed the lookout each fire season, 1997 to 2016.
Registered with the National Historic Lookout Register, April 24, 2009.
Cab wrapped in fire-retardant material as a precaution against a nearby wildfire; staff moved temporarily to Salmon Mountain.
Cab wrapped in fire-retardant material again; staff evacuated by helicopter.
Idaho Fire Lookouts says Mark and Rhett Moak staffed the lookout again.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Sources give 1930 for the first lookout, a platform in a tree, and 1960 for the current R-6 cab on its concrete base. They describe different structures on the same site, as the record's own conflict note suggests.

notes_for_editor: Disputed: the L-4 date (1934 on firelookout.com and Forest Lookouts; 1940 on the register and Idaho Fire Lookouts), the base date (1959 base build vs 1960 completion), and the wilderness name (register: Frank Church neighbour; Keeping Watch: Selway-Bitterroot). Elevation: the register's 8,116 ft (2,474 m) matches the record; Idaho Fire Lookouts gives 6727′, not used. Access level omitted: drive-up is supported, but no source states public or closed status, so a visitor check is advised. The 2025 staffing rests on one source. The Keeping Watch page says 'Built: 1930', which is the first platform, not the current cab. No source read describes the lookout as burned, moved or abandoned. Record height_m 3.0 is not confirmed; sources give a 10-foot base only. No new photos recorded.
